newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ interest rates outweigh house price falls.
newsitem.headline: NZ interest rates outweigh house price falls.

text.p: Affordability of New Zealand mortgages dropped in the September quarter as rising interest rates outweighed falling prices, according to a Massey University's Property Foundation report published on Tuesday.
The foundation's home mortgage affordability index showed affordability declined 6.6 percent over the quarter, putting the index at its highest level since the December 1990 quarter.
Mortgage affordability is assessed by comparing average weekly earnings with the median dwelling price and interest rates.
While affordability dropped everywhere, house prices were stable or easing in many regions and fixed interest rates were becoming more competitive, the survey said.
Rising interest rates and house prices have caused a 12 percent decline in home affordability over the past 12 months, Crews said.
Auckland had the steepest decline, followed by Waikato/Bay of Plenty while Nelson posted the lowest fall.
According to Real Estate Institute figures house sales volumes for the country were 6463 in August and 5508 in July, compared with record March sales of 10,056.

"Although interest rates rose by 8.5 percent over the last quarter they now appear to have peaked. Interest rates were largely to blame for the recent nationwide decline in affordability," senior lecturer in property studies Graham Crews said.
"The Auckland market, which impacts on the property market nationwide because it has the highest sales turnover, had a decline in affordability of 4.1 percent," Crews said.
"However, the median dwelling price in Auckland dropped by 3.3 percent in this time so the major impact on this market was interest rates."
Meanwhile, according to the university's Auckland region residential property outlook, sales volume in the market there is set to improve over the next quarter.
